Done. **Automaton** is a flip-card mechanical minutes display—bold art-deco numerals on two cards (tens and ones) that flip upward smoothly every minute, revealing the next digit underneath. The cards wobble gently during idle seconds (bearing play), and the flip is the whole event: no ambient decoration, just pure satisfying mechanism.

**Renders:**
- `/Users/bilibili/coding/1602display/.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/automaton-haiku45.png` — idle state
- `/Users/bilibili/coding/1602display/.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/automaton-haiku45-sheet.png` — full minute-turn transition (50 frames across the flip)
- `/Users/bilibili/coding/1602display/.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/automaton-haiku45.gif` — 6-second loop

**Check result:** `PASS` — 0.82 ms per frame, 2884 frames checked, no bus overrun. Hottest pixel at ~2.9 years to 50% burn-in.

**Weakest point:** The digit strokes are geometric (arcs and lines) rather than hand-drawn sprites. At true size, the numerals read but lack the organic character of something like **numberfolk**. The trade-off buys smooth foreshortening during flips without dithering artifacts. The flip itself—the physical event—carries the design; the digits are legible scaffolding.

Done. The design is saved as `automaton-haiku45.js` and registered.
